name: web
description: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, gRPC, WebSockets and server-sent events across a 50 ms path (pathlab): ALPN and h2c, a page of 20 resources over 1 vs 6 HTTP/1.1 connections vs one HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connection, application head-of-line blocking, multiplexed streams in a decrypted capture, HPACK savings, QUIC 1-RTT, resumption and 0-RTT, transport head-of-line blocking from one lost packet in HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3 (and QPACK's own), UDP blocked, gRPC on the wire (trailers, status in HTTP 200, deadlines, streaming, no reflection, an HTTP/1.1 proxy breaking it), the WebSocket handshake and frames, a load balancer idle timeout vs pings, and SSE through a buffering proxy

nodes.name: router
setup: ip tuntap add dev pl-ab mode tun && ip tuntap add dev pl-ba mode tun && ip link set pl-ab up && ip link set pl-ba up && sysctl -qw net.ipv4.conf.pl-ab.rp_filter=0 net.ipv4.conf.pl-ba.rp_filter=0 && ip rule add iif eth0 table 100 && ip route add default dev pl-ab table 100 && ip rule add iif eth1 table 101 && ip route add default dev pl-ba table 101

checks.name: ALPN: curl offers h2 and http/1.1 in the ClientHello, the server picks h2; the response advertises HTTP/3 in Alt-Svc
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; curl -sv --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -o /dev/null https://web.test/ 2>&1 | grep -iE 'ALPN|^< HTTP|alt-svc'

checks.name: the same server with --http1.1: ALPN agrees on http/1.1
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; curl -sv --http1.1 --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -o /dev/null https://web.test/ 2>&1 | grep -iE 'ALPN|^< HTTP'

checks.name: cleartext port 80: HTTP/1.1 by default; HTTP/2 only with prior knowledge (h2c) — no TLS, so no ALPN to negotiate it
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; curl -s http://web.test/; curl -s --http2-prior-knowledge http://web.test/

checks.name: a page and 20 small resources (2 KB each): HTTP/1.1 on 1 connection, on 6 (a browser's limit), HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 on one
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; ${BIN}/weblab get -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -proto h1 -conns 1 -page -n 21 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000' | tail -1; ${BIN}/weblab get -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -proto h1 -conns 6 -page -n 21 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000' | tail -1; ${BIN}/weblab get -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -proto h2  -page -n 21 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000' | tail -1; ${PYTHON} ${LABS}/http3/h3lab.py get --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem --page -n 21 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000' | tail -1

checks.name: head-of-line blocking in HTTP/1.1: a fast request queued behind a slow one (1 s) on the same connection waits; HTTP/2 answers it at once
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; ${BIN}/weblab get -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -proto h1 -conns 1 -stagger 10ms 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000&delay=1s' 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000'; ${BIN}/weblab get -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -proto h2 -stagger 10ms 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000&delay=1s' 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000'

checks.name: capture six 20 KB responses on one HTTP/2 connection, with the client's TLS key log
decrypted: one TCP connection, client streams 1, 3, 5 …, and packets that carry frames of several streams at once (interleaving)
run:
tshark -r ${EVIDENCE}/h2-mux.pcap -o tls.keylog_file:${EVIDENCE}/client-keys.log -Y http2 -T fields -e tcp.stream -e ip.src -e http2.streamid -e http2.type 2>/dev/null | awk '{conns[$1]=1; n=split($3,s,","); split($4,t,","); k=0; delete seen; for(i=1;i<=n;i++){ if (s[i]>0) {ids[s[i]]=1; if(!(s[i] in seen)){seen[s[i]]=1;k++}} } if (k>1) mixed++} END{printf "TCP connections: %d
HTTP/2 streams:", length(conns); m=0; for (i in ids) if (i+0>m) m=i+0; for (i=1;i<=m;i+=2) if (i in ids) printf " %d", i; printf "
packets carrying frames of more than one stream: %d
", mixed}'
expect_contains: packets carrying frames of more than one stream:

checks.name: HPACK: 100 responses' headers cost 588 bytes over HTTP/2 vs 111 bytes each over HTTP/1.1
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; h2load -n 100 -c 1 -m 10 'https://web.test/obj?size=100' 2>&1 | grep -E 'Application protocol|traffic:'; h2load --h1 -n 100 -c 1 'https://web.test/obj?size=100' 2>&1 | grep -E 'Application protocol|traffic:'

checks.name: nghttp shows the HTTP/2 frames: SETTINGS both ways, the request HEADERS (pseudo-headers), the response HEADERS and DATA
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; nghttp -nv 'https://web.test/obj?size=100' 2>&1 | grep -E 'send|recv|^ +:|SETTINGS_'

checks.name: first byte: HTTP/2 needs TCP + TLS + request = 3 round trips; HTTP/3 new = 2, resumed = 2, 0-RTT = 1 (the request rides in the first flight)
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/ticket.pkl; curl -s -o /dev/null --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -w 'HTTP/2: tcp %{time_connect} tls %{time_appconnect} first byte %{time_starttransfer}\n' 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000'; for z in '' '' --zero-rtt; do ${PYTHON} ${LABS}/http3/h3lab.py get --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem --ticket ${EVIDENCE}/ticket.pkl $z 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000' | grep -E '^(stream|handshake)'; done

checks.name: capture a 0-RTT HTTP/3 request

run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; ${PYTHON} ${LABS}/http3/h3lab.py get --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem --ticket ${EVIDENCE}/ticket.pkl --zero-rtt 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000' | tail -1

checks.name: the client's first flight: an Initial (ClientHello) and a 0-RTT packet (the request) leave together, before any reply
run: tshark -r ${EVIDENCE}/h3-0rtt.pcap -T fields -e frame.time_relative -e ip.src -e udp.length -e quic.long.packet_type 2>/dev/null | head -6 | awk '{k=split($4,t,","); n=""; for(i=1;i<=k;i++) n=n (t[i]==0?" Initial":t[i]==1?" 0-RTT":t[i]==2?" Handshake":" "t[i]); if (k==0) n=" 1-RTT (short header)"; printf "%8.1f ms  %-15s %5d bytes %s\n", $1*1000, $2, $3, n}'

checks.name: one lost packet (the first resource packet; pathlab drop_big=4): HTTP/2 holds EVERY stream until it is retransmitted; HTTP/3 delivers the others (QPACK's dynamic table can re-create the blocking)
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; for k in 0 4; do ${BIN}/pathlab set -c 198.18.110.1:9911 drop_big=$k >/dev/null; ${BIN}/weblab get -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -proto h2 -page -n 11 'https://web.test/obj?size=3000' | awk '/done/{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="done") print $(i+1)}' | awk -v L="HTTP/2, drop $k" '{a[NR]=$1} END{s=""; for(i=2;i<=NR;i++) s=s" "a[i]; print L": page "a[1]" ms | resources done at"s" ms"}'; ${BIN}/pathlab set -c 198.18.110.1:9911 drop_big=$k >/dev/null; ${PYTHON} ${LABS}/http3/h3lab.py get --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem --page -n 11 'https://web.test/obj?size=3000' | awk '/done/{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="done") print $(i+1)}' | sort -n | awk -v L="HTTP/3 + QPACK dynamic table, drop $k" '{a[NR]=$1} END{s=""; for(i=2;i<=NR;i++) s=s" "a[i]; print L": page "a[1]" ms | resources done at"s" ms"}'; ${BIN}/pathlab set -c 198.18.110.1:9911 drop_big=$k >/dev/null; ${PYTHON} ${LABS}/http3/h3lab.py get --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem --qpack-table 0 --page -n 11 'https://web.test/obj?size=3000' | awk '/done/{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="done") print $(i+1)}' | sort -n | awk -v L="HTTP/3, no QPACK dynamic table, drop $k" '{a[NR]=$1} END{s=""; for(i=2;i<=NR;i++) s=s" "a[i]; print L": page "a[1]" ms | resources done at"s" ms"}'; done
expect_contains: HTTP/3 + QPACK dynamic table, drop 4: page
HTTP/3, no QPACK dynamic table, drop 4: page

checks.name: pathlab counted the three targeted drops
block UDP 443 on the path, as many firewalls do
HTTP/3 gets no answer at all (a browser then uses HTTP/2 over TCP, which still works)
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; ${PYTHON} ${LABS}/http3/h3lab.py get --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem --timeout 3 'https://web.test/obj?size=2000'; curl -s -o /dev/null --cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -w 'TCP fallback: HTTP/%{http_version} %{http_code}\n' https://web.test/

checks.name: unblock UDP 443
a gRPC call is an HTTP/2 POST: content-type application/grpc, te: trailers, a 5-byte prefix + protobuf; the result is in the TRAILERS
grpcurl, the standard client, against the same hand-built server — cleartext and TLS
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; grpcurl -import-path ${LABS}/grpc -proto echo.proto -plaintext -d '"hello"' web.test:80 course.Echo/Echo && grpcurl -import-path ${LABS}/grpc -proto echo.proto -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -d '"over tls"' web.test:443 course.Echo/Echo

checks.name: an error is still HTTP 200: grpc-status 3 (INVALID_ARGUMENT) in a trailers-only response
expect_contains: INVALID_ARGUMENT (3) value must not be empty

checks.name: curl sees only HTTP: 200 OK — the failure (12, UNIMPLEMENTED) is in grpc-status; HTTP status alone says nothing about a gRPC call
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; curl -s --http2-prior-knowledge -D - -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'content-type: application/grpc' -H 'te: trailers' --data-binary '' http://web.test/course.Echo/Nope | grep -iE '^HTTP|grpc'

checks.name: deadlines: grpcurl -max-time 0.5 sends grpc-timeout (what is LEFT of 500 ms after connecting); the server stops when it expires
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; grpcurl -import-path ${LABS}/grpc -proto echo.proto -plaintext -max-time 0.5 -d '"slow"' web.test:80 course.Echo/Slow; sleep 0.3; grep -a 'Slow' ${EVIDENCE}/service-server-web.log | tail -2

checks.name: server streaming: five messages on one HTTP/2 stream, 300 ms apart, then the trailers
no reflection: `grpcurl list` needs the server's reflection service; with the .proto file every call above still works
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; grpcurl -plaintext web.test:80 list
expect_contains: server does not support the reflection API

checks.name: through a proxy that forwards over HTTP/1.1 (an ALB target group on HTTP1): the server answers HTTP 505, which gRPC reports as UNKNOWN; over h2c it works
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; grpcurl -import-path ${LABS}/grpc -proto echo.proto -plaintext -d '"via h1"' web.test:8080 course.Echo/Echo; ${BIN}/weblab grpc web.test:8080 course.Echo/Echo 'via h1' | tail -2; grpcurl -import-path ${LABS}/grpc -proto echo.proto -plaintext -d '"via h2c"' web.test:8083 course.Echo/Echo

checks.name: the WebSocket upgrade: 101 Switching Protocols, Sec-WebSocket-Accept derived from the key; client frames masked (6 bytes of header), server frames not (2)
expect_contains: 11 bytes on the wire (2 header + 4 mask + 5 payload)

checks.name: RFC 6455's own example key gives its documented accept value
through a relay with a 5 s idle timeout (a load balancer), a quiet WebSocket is cut after 5 s
expect_contains: connection closed by the peer after 5

checks.name: the same, with a ping every 2 s: the connection survives
server-sent events: one event every 500 ms on a plain HTTP response; reconnecting with Last-Event-ID resumes after it
run: unset HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; ${BIN}/weblab sse -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem 'https://web.test/events?n=3&every=500ms'; ${BIN}/weblab sse -cacert ${EVIDENCE}/ca.pem -last-id 3 'https://web.test/events?n=2&every=500ms'

checks.name: through a proxy that buffers responses, the same events arrive together at the end

requires.${PYTHON}: create the course venv: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r labs/requirements.txt (HTTP/3 needs aioquic)
